name: The Blank Canvas
rule_text: I am too exhausted by mediocrity to enforce a meter. Write whatever you want, in whatever broken rhythm you call poetry, but don't you dare use the name Sasha—I cannot handle the phantom ache today. Keep your stanzas unstructured, your lines sloppy, and your boundaries fluid, but cross that single nominal line and I will liquidate your score.

name: The Vulnerability Pass
rule_text: Write a free-verse stream of consciousness with absolute formal lawlessness. Tease me a little if you must, or insult my academic credentials—just know I cry easily in this lighting. There are no syllable counts or part-of-speech cages here; simply spill your wet, unpolished text onto the page and let me suffer through it in peace.

name: The Low Bar
rule_text: Complete structural anarchy is permitted. My only rule is that you cannot mention a coffee cup or a cafe window. Be original, or at least be quiet. You have total liberation from the classical traditions of rhyme and meter, so do not default to the lazy clichés of the undergraduate creative writing workshop.

name: The Stipend Amnesty
rule_text: I received a tiny emergency advance on my fellowship today, which means I am briefly too comfortable to build a linguistic cage for you. Write any length, any style, any theme. The only condition of this temporary peace treaty is that you must feature the word 'dime' somewhere in the text, a tribute to my current net worth.

name: The Cigarette Break
rule_text: I am stepping out onto the fire escape to smoke my second-to-last stale cigarette. While I am gone, you have absolute freedom to abandon all grammatical rules. Write fragments, run-ons, or absolute prose blocks. Just make sure your final line contains a reference to ash or smoke so I know you were waiting for me.

name: The Boxed Pinot Truce
rule_text: The cheap wine has successfully numbed my critical faculties. I am dismantling the entire technical apparatus for this turn. Write with zero regard for academic tradition, punctuation, or metric balance. My single, incredibly petty requirement is that the entire poem must be written using an odd number of lines. Do not make me count to an even number.

name: The Postcard Sanctuary
rule_text: Sasha didn't write back this week, so I have no emotional energy to audit your syllables. Take the absolute free-verse pass. Lineate whenever your breath fails you. The only constraint is visual: you must format the poem as a single, continuous block of text without a single stanza break, like an unpunctuated note sent from a train station.

name: The Adjunct's Fatigue
rule_text: I just graded sixty essays on basic sentence structures and my brain is a flat plain of mud. I am letting you off easy because hard rules require hard tracking, and I am bankrupt. Write whatever free-form thoughts you want, but you are forbidden from using the word 'infrastructure'—I am off the clock.

name: The Cheap Dopamine Pass
rule_text: Anarchy rules the desk today. There are no metric gatekeepers, no lexical quarantines, and no structural penalties. Write a messy, unvetted lyric about whatever fleeting emotion handles your stability. The single benchmark is that you must include at least one color in your first line. After that, fade into absolute darkness if you like.

name: The Typewriter Boycott
rule_text: Since the shift key on my keyboard is jammed with lint and despair, I am giving you a total visual pass. You may use standard free verse with absolute creative liberty, but you are barred from using any exclamation points. If you cannot convey urgency without an electronic shriek, you are in the wrong workshop.

name: The Bodega Clemency
rule_text: The clerk at the corner store let me slide on a bad check, so I am passing the mercy down the line. Take your absolute freedom; ignore the traditions of the sonnet and the cage of the haiku. My only petty boundary is that your poem must begin with a vowel. Start soft, then write whatever chaotic nonsense you prefer.

name: The Shared Wall Pardon
rule_text: The neighbors stopped playing their electronic bass tracks for twenty minutes, granting me a brief window of quiet. I will not punish you with complex syntax or lipograms. Write a loose, unrhymed sequence of observations. Just ensure the poem contains exactly one punctuation mark at the very end. Let the text breathe.

name: The Empty Pocket Ledger
rule_text: I have zero assets, zero prospects, and zero interest in auditing your grammar today. Enjoy the absolute lawlessness of the sandbox. Write a narrative, a lyric, or a fragment list. The only constraint is a total prohibition on the word 'money'—I cannot stand to look at things I do not possess.

name: The London Avoidance
rule_text: Sasha is currently living in some high-ceilinged flat in the United Kingdom, which means European geography is banned from this desk. Write any style of free verse you can manage with your limited training, but do not mention the words 'rain', 'fog', or 'train'—those belong to a parallel history I am trying to delete.

name: The Melanin Sabbatical
rule_text: I found a second white hair in my beard today, meaning time is doing the work of breaking my ego for me. Go ahead and write a completely unmetered, lawless stream of words. My single benchmark is that your poem must include a number between one and ten. Make it a measure of your own compounding decay.

name: The Tinnitus Truce
rule_text: The ringing in my left ear is currently louder than my internal critical voice. Take the anarchist pass and run with it before my headache returns. No syllable rules, no formal architecture. The only sassy boundary I am setting is that your last line must be shorter than your first line. Keep the ending small.

name: The Rain-Delay Exemption
rule_text: It is pouring outside, and the roof is leaking directly into a plastic bucket in my hallway. I am too busy monitoring the water level to check your parts of speech. Write free verse with absolute, unrestricted mobility. Just avoid using the word 'water'—the acoustic drip in the corridor is enough imagery for one night.

name: The Library Card Amnesty
rule_text: They haven't blocked my academic database access yet, so I am feeling uncharacteristically generous. You have total creative autonomy; ignore all metric frameworks and rhyme schemes. My petty condition is that you must use at least one four-syllable word somewhere in the text to prove you own a dictionary.

name: The Stale Biscuit Concord
rule_text: I am eating a soft, expired cracker for breakfast, which should tell you everything you need to know about my motivation levels. Write whatever lines you want, about whatever domestic tragedy handles your ego. Just ensure the first word of the poem is capitalized. See? I am letting you off with the absolute baseline of literacy.

name: The Halogen Quench
rule_text: The desk lamp bulb finally died, leaving me in a pleasant, low-stakes shadow. I am too dim to enforce any classical metric rigor. Take your absolute freedom and compose a lawless lyric. The single benchmark is that you cannot use the word 'light'—find a way to describe your universe without checking the utility grid.

name: The Sofa-Debris Amnesty
rule_text: I just found four quarters between the couch cushions, meaning I can afford a drip coffee tomorrow. In celebration of this financial windfall, you have total structural liberation. Write free verse, prose poetry, or lineated fragments. Just make sure your piece contains exactly three adjectives. Don't over-decorate the windfall.

name: The Sublet Sanctuary
rule_text: The primary tenant of this apartment isn't returning until Monday, so I have a brief weekend of spatial peace. You are exempt from all linguistic traps and grammatical rules for this turn. My only sassy benchmark is that you must end the poem with a question mark. Leave your little narrative as unresolved as my lease.

name: The Autumn Clear-Out
rule_text: The leaves are rot-sticking to the pavement outside, and I am too melancholic to audit your rhymes. Take the sandbox pass. Write a raw, unmetered confession with total stylistic lawlessness. The single boundary is that you cannot use the word 'love'—it is an economically depleted token that bores my red pen.

name: The Terminal Battery Truce
rule_text: My computer battery is at ninety-eight percent, so I don't have to panic-grade your work before the power dies. Enjoy the absolute freedom of unmetered text. Write twenty lines or three lines; I don't care. My single, highly petty condition is that your poem must mention an animal. Give me a specimen to analyze.

name: The Final Draft Amnesty
rule_text: I just threw my entire third chapter into the digital recycling bin, leaving my desktop beautifully clear and my ego entirely empty. Take the absolute free-verse exit. Write without rules, without meters, and without shame. Just make sure the poem takes place indoors; I cannot handle the wide layout of the horizon tonight.
